metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Ruled out for Week 5
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest at Jacksonville.
metadata.analysis: Barkley didn't practice this week in the wake of suffering a right hamstring injury this past Sunday against the Rams, so his lack of availability for Week 5 doesn't come as a surprise. With Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve, it'll be the Will Shipley show out of the Eagles backfield Sunday, while Dameon Pierce also is on hand for RB reps that linger, and Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele are options to be elevated from the practice squad. Barkley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Oct. 18 versus the Panthers.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) officially ruled out Sunday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Barkley will miss at least one game as expected. Will Shipley becomes an RB2 as the likely lead back in the backfield. The Eagles also elevated Dameon Pierce to the active roster.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) not seen at practice Friday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley was not seen at practice on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley will figure to be ruled out when the injury report is released. He remains week-to-week. Will Shipley should lead the Eagles backfield on Sunday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Remains absent Friday
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, EJ Smith reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley hasn't practiced this week and isn't likely to play against the Jaguars on Sunday, leaving Will Shipley, Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue as Philadelphia's backfield options for Week 5. Shipley is the favorite to start and get most of the snaps.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Ruled Out for Week 5
metadata.description: After not practicing all week, Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, according to John Clark of NBC Sports. Backup Tank Bigsby (abdomen) also had core-muscle surgery and is on Injured Reserve, which means that Will Shipley is set up to handle the bulk of the backfield duties this weekend against Jacksonville. Former Houston Texans RB Dameon Pierce was added to the active 53-man roster this week and will help handle change-of-pace duties on Sunday in his first game with Philly. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury in last week's loss to the Los Angeles Rams, but the good news is that his injury is not believed to be long-term, so hopefully he will have a shot to return for Week 6 tilt at home against the Carolina Panthers next Sunday. The 29-year-old is still searching for his first touchdown of the year, but he is averaging a healthy 5.1 yards per carry and has 182 rushing yards on his 36 rushing attempts through four games. Shipley should at least be considered an RB3/flex against the Jags.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Another DNP on Thursday
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) officially didn't practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley has yet to log any on-field work since tweaking his right hamstring on his fourth offensive snap this past Sunday against the Rams. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Barkley is considered week-to-week, and the Eagles can make a ruling on the running back's status for a Week 5 road matchup with the Jaguars on Friday's injury report. Will Shipley is poised for a workhorse role out of Philadelphia's backfield this weekend assuming Barkley indeed is ruled out.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Not Expected to Play in Week 5 in London
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was injured in the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday and is now not expected to play in Week 5 in London this Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Barkley's hamstring is not considered a major injury, but he is considered week-to-week and has missed the first two practices of the week. Backup Tank Bigsby (abdomen) had core-muscle surgery and was placed on Injured Reserve, so it is suddenly looking like Will Shipley will be the Eagles' primary option out of the backfield this weekend against the Jags. The Eagles added Dameon Pierce to their active roster this week amidst the injuries at the position, but he will likely take a back seat to Shipley this weekend if, in fact, Barkley is eventually ruled out. Although it is not official yet, fantasy managers should move Barkley to their bench this week. The three-time Pro Bowler has yet to find the end zone through four games in 2026, but he is averaging 5.1 yards per carry on his 36 rushing attempts in his third year in Philly.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) not seen practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley was not seen practicing on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley remains unlikely to play this week on Sunday. Will Shipley appears likely to be the lead back against the Jaguars in London.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Not seen at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't present during the open portion of Thursday's practice, Tim McManus of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley appears as if he'll go down as a non-participant for a second session in a row to kick off Week 5 prep, something that'll be confirmed once the Eagles post Thursday's injury report. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Barkley currently is viewed as week-to-week due to the hamstring issue that knocked him out of this past Sunday's game against the Rams after just four offensive snaps, so the running back's continued likely lack of activity isn't unexpected.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Not Seen at Thursday's Practice
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was among the players that ESPN's Tim McManus did not see during a brief portion of practice open to the media on Thursday. Barkley injured his hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams and is now very questionable to play in London on Sunday in Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Tank Bigsby (abdomen) is having core-muscle surgery and landed on Injured Reserve this week, so he will be out for at least four games. The Eagles' backfield depth is going to be tested if Barkley does not get cleared to play this weekend. Philly added veteran back Dameon Pierce to their active 53-man roster this week for extra depth, but if Barkley is inactive, it will likely be Will Shipley seeing most of the backfield work. Barkley sitting out on Sunday would put Shipley immediately into flex territory against the Jaguars. A second straight day of missed practice on Thursday would put Barkley on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5. If he is a true game-time decision, the good news is that fantasy managers will know early on Sunday whether he is active.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - No practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) officially didn't practice Wednesday
metadata.analysis: Barkley lasted just four offensive snaps before exiting this past Sunday's loss to the Rams in the first quarter due to a hamstring issue. Head coach Nick Sirianni remained mum Monday regarding Barkley's status, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic, though Ian Rapoport of NFL Network later reported that the running back is considered week-to-week with an injury that's not deemed to be long term. As a result, Barkley's lack of activity Wednesday isn't a shock, and if he indeed sits out Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London, he likely will pass off the No. 1 spot in the Eagles backfield to Will Shipley, with Dameon Pierce backing him up.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) not practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley did not practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley remains week-to-week. He is unlikely to play on Sunday against the Jaguars.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Absent from practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: With Barkley already considered week-to-week coming out of Sunday's loss to the Rams, his absence from Wednesday's session is no surprise. Barkley should be considered closer to doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce are currently in line to handle backfield duties after Tank Bigsby (abdomen) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Not at Wednesday's Practice
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen at practice on Wednesday after suffering a hamstring injury in the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, according to Brooks Kubena of The Athletic. The Eagles are labeling Barkley as week-to-week after his injury on Sunday, and with backup Tank Bigsby (abdomen) going on Injured Reserve, Will Shipley is in line for a significant backfield workload for Philly on Sunday in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars if Barkley is officially ruled out on Friday. Fantasy managers should not plan on having Barkley available to them this weekend after what has been a disappointing first four games in 2026 so far. The Pro Bowl RB has yet to find the end zone and has carried the ball 36 times for 182 yards (5.1 yards per carry) while adding four catches for only eight yards. Barkley's efficiency has been strong, but he also missed time in a game with a stinger and now looks likely to miss at least one game for the Eagles. The team also added Dameon Pierce for backfield depth, and he could have a decent role right away this weekend if Barkley cannot go.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) considered week-to-week
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley is considered week-to-week with his hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: It is not believed to be a serious injury, but Barkley will likely be sidelined in Week 5 against the Jaguars.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Deemed week-to-week due to hamstring issue
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) is considered week-to-week, though the Eagles don't view the injury as long term, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: After exiting early in Sunday's loss to the Rams with the hamstring issue, Barkley now appears likely to miss at least some time. However, the Eagles -- and Barkley's fantasy managers -- can breathe a sign of relief since the injury doesn't appear likely to sideline the star running back for a substantial period of time. With Tank Bigsby (abdomen) expected to land on IR, Philadelphia's backfield is down to just Will Shipley among healthy options on the active roster. The Eagles will likely turn to one or more of Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele from the practice squad for Week 5 and potentially beyond.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Status uncertain with injured hamstring
metadata.description: Coach Nick Sirianni said, "We'll see," Monday afternoon when asked about Barkley's new hamstring injury, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports. "We'll have more answers Wednesday for you probably with that stuff," Sirianni added.
metadata.analysis: Barkley injured his hamstring in the opening minutes of Sunday's eventual loss to the Rams and wasn't able to return to action. Tank Bigsby was the biggest beneficiary of Barkley's absence, but he exited late with a lower-body issue that will require core muscle surgery and a stint on IR, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. With Barkley's status uncertain, the Eagles currently host one healthy running back (Will Shipley) on the active roster, while Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are options to be bumped up from the practice squad.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley "Unlikely" to Play in Week 5
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is "unlikely" to play in his team's Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Philly's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and is considered week-to-week. The Eagles also lost top backup running back Tank Bigsby (core) in Week 4, as he suffered a core muscle injury and has been placed on Injured Reserve. Without Barkley and Bigsby against Jacksonville, Eagles RB3 Will Shipley appears likely to be the team's lead back. McLane also notes running backs Dameon Pierce, Jaydon Blue, and Carson Steele are all on the Eagles' practice squad and could be candidates for elevation to the active roster in Week 5.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Considered Week-to-Week With Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is considered week-to-week with the hamstring injury that he suffered in Sunday's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, according to the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo. Barkley's injury is not considered to be a long-term injury, but his availability for the Week 5 contest this Sunday's game on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars is very much in question. Fantasy managers should prepare for the worst, which would probably mean Barkley missing a couple of weeks. Backup Tank Bigsby took over early in Sunday's loss to the Rams, but he suffered an injury as well and will go on Injured Reserve after having core-muscle surgery. With Barkley and Bigsby banged up, Will Shipley will be one of the most popular waiver-wire pickups going into Week 5. Barkley, who led the NFL with 2,005 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns in 2024 in his first year in Philly, has averaged 5.1 yards per carry for 182 rushing yards in four games in 2026, but he has yet to find the end zone. He has added only four catches for eight yards as a receiver. We will have a better idea of Barkley's status for this weekend against the Jags once the Eagles begin practicing on Wednesday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) without update on injury
metadata.description: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he'll "have more answers Wednesday" on Saquon Barkley's hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: Barkley went down early in Sunday's game against the Rams. His status is up in the air heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley's Injury Status to be Updated on Wednesday
metadata.description: When asked about running back Saquon Barkley's hamstring injury that he suffered in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams, Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not have any real answers on Monday, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic. "We'll see. We'll have more answers Wednesday for you probably with that stuff," Sirianni said. The Eagles' backfield is suddenly very thin after Barkley was injured early in the Week 4 game. Backup Tank Bigsby (core) took over, but he was also injured and is heading to Injured Reserve due to a core-muscle injury that will require surgery. Will Shipley would become the RB1 for the Eagles this weekend on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars if Barkley is unable to play. Behind Shipley, other options for the Eagles' backfield would be Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce, and Carson Steele. Fantasy managers should consider Barkley to be questionable right now for the Week 5 game in Jacksonville. Before getting hurt, Barkley had only two carries for eight yards and caught his only target for a two-yard gain against the Rams.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley suffers hamstring injury Sunday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley rushed the ball two times for eight yards and caught one pass for two yards before leaving Sunday's loss to the Rams with a hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday's loss to the Rams. The severity of the injury is unknown at this point, so fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his status throughout the week. Tank Bigsby will be primed for more work if the veteran has to miss any time.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Set for tests on injured hamstring
metadata.description: Barkley will undergo further testing Monday, but the right hamstring injury he sustained in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams isn't believed to be "overly serious," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley carried twice for eight yards and hauled in his lone target for a two-yard reception before departing Sunday's contest in the first quarter with the hamstring issue. Though injuries have now resulted in Barkley playing limited snaps in two of the Eagles' last three games, the team seems optimistic that his latest setback on the health front isn't anything major. His upcoming medical tests should provide a clearer picture of his health heading into a Week 5 matchup with the Jaguars next Sunday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley to Undergo Tests, Injury Does Not Appear Serious
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is set to undergo further testing, but it does not appear to be overly serious, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Barkley suffered a hamstring injury on the second drive of the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. In four games this season, he has 36 carries for 182 yards and added just eight receiving yards on four catches, leaving two of those games early due to injury. With Barkley out, running backs Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley carried the load, with Bigsby leading the backfield with 14 carries. However, Bigsby left for the locker room in the fourth quarter, and there's no word on the severity of his undisclosed injury. The Eagles travel to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5, where it's unclear whether Barkley will make the trip.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Won't return Sunday
metadata.description: Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Rams, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley tweaked his hamstring on a six-yard run in the first quarter, and the injury is severe enough for the star running back to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's game. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley will handle backfield duties the rest of the way in Barkley's absence.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Week 4 contest between the Philadelphia Eagles and Los Angeles Rams according to Ian Rapoport.
metadata.analysis: Barkley will remain sidelined after suffering the hamstring injury in the first half Sunday, carrying the ball twice for eight yards and catching his lone target for two yards prior to exiting. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley take over backfield duties for head coach Nick Sirianni.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) questionable to return
metadata.description: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley is questionable to return agains the Rams with a hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: Barkley was able to walk off the field slowly under his own power after a rushing attempt in the first quarter. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley will likely split time out of the backfield if Barkley is unable to return.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Injures hamstring in Week 4
metadata.description: Barkley suffered a hamstring injury during Sunday's game against the Rams, Olivia Reiner of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley walked slowly to the sideline after a six-yard run in the first quarter and visited the medical tent before making his way to the locker room. During Barkley's absence, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are the candidates for reps out of the Eagles backfield.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Enters medical tent in first quarter
metadata.description: Barkley (lower body) made his way to the sideline slowly and then entered the medical tent during the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Rams, Olivia Reiner of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: After a six-yard run on the Eagles' second possession, the aforementioned situation befell Barkley. For as long as Barkley is sidelined, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley will man Philadelphia's backfield.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Ruled Out With Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams, according to Adam Schefter. Barkley pulled up after a six-yard run in the first quarter and grabbed at his right hamstring before heading to the medical tent. He later went to the locker room and was initially listed as questionable to return. Barkley finishes with two carries for eight yards. Tank Bigsby was the first back onto the field after Barkley left, with Will Shipley also available behind him. Philadelphia has not provided any further information yet on the severity of Barkley's hamstring injury.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Seen Hobbling After Run vs. Rams, Questionable to Return
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable to return against the Los Angeles Rams due to a hamstring injury, according to the team. He was seen hobbling after a six-yard run against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic. Following the run, Barkley was spotted limping on the sideline and then went to the blue medical tent. Running back Tank Bigsby has entered the lineup in Barkley's absence. Will Shipley is also available in the backfield for the Eagles.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Looking for First Breakout Performance of 2025 in Week 4
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley hasn't found the end zone yet this season and has been targeted just six times through three games -- he hauled in three of those passes for a massive six yards. That's got him ranked as the RB33 overall in fantasy football through three games, which is a clip that seems impossible. But the Eagles offensive line has taken multiple huge steps back since Barkley's insane 2024 season. He's averaging over five yards per carry, but the lack of a receiving role and inability to score so far has made that a moot point. Week 4 might not see things get much better, as the Eagles will face the Los Angeles Rams, who have an explosive passing offense. They'll likely be able to run up the score, preventing the Eagles from relying heavily on the run game and forcing them into a pass-heavy game script. Barkley has not been start-worthy through three games, as he has just single-digit PPR fantasy points in each, though you have to think he has upside for more. He's a startable player as a low-end RB2 for now, but fantasy managers are understandably nervous about his potential to be a league-losing draft pick.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley's Lack of Valuable Touches Affecting his Fantasy Value
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley has gotten off to a slow start to his 2026 season. In three games, Barkley has 34 carries for 174 yards and no touchdowns, along with three receptions for six yards. His current average of 6.5 half-PPR fantasy points per game ranks him RB37 on a per-game basis. While he's been efficient, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, his limited receiving and goal-line work with the Eagles' patented "tush push" have hurt his fantasy value early in the season. With tough matchups against the Los Angeles Rams and the Jacksonville Jaguars in the next two weeks, Barkley may be unable to rebound. Fantasy managers should remain wary of Barkley's ceiling given his lack of valuable touches, though he remains a strong RB2 moving forward.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley runs for 82 yards in Week 3
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley carried the ball 15 times for 82 yards and lost two yards on his lone catch in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Barkley was able to suit up and lead the Philadelphia backfield one week after suffering a shoulder stinger. He looked good in the contest, averaging 5.5 yards per carry for the Eagles. Still looking for his first touchdown of the season, Barkley has now gained 174 yards while catching three passes for six yards through three games. He will be a solid fantasy option in Week 4 against the Rams.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Solid numbers in double-digit loss
metadata.description: Barkley rushed 15 times for 82 yards and secured one of two targets for minus-2 yards in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Barkley was a rare bright spot for an otherwise moribund Eagles offense, showing no ill effects from the stinger that cost him substantial time in a Week 2 win over the Titans. The star running back got his night started on the right foot with a 12-yard run on Philadelphia's opening possession and a nine-yarder on the second drive that was wiped out by a holding penalty. Barkley would go on to add another four rushes of seven or more yards, including a game-long 17-yard scamper. Barkley has yet to top 15 carries in any of the first three games of the season, but he's been highly efficient while averaging 5.1 yards per carry and posting four runs of 10-plus yards overall. Barkley and the Eagles have a tall order on their Week 4 ledger, however, as the Rams come to town Sunday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) off injury report for Eagles
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley (stinger) is off of the injury report and cleared to play for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Chicago Bears Monday night according to Mike Garafolo.
metadata.analysis: Barkley is good to go after logging full practice sessions to end the week for head coach Nick Sirianni, boosting a Philadelphia rushing attack that will look to take advantage of a susceptible Bears defense Monday night.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Dealing with Stinger, But Will Play in Good Matchup vs. Bears
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (neck/shoulder) suffered a stinger injury in a 24-20 Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans, but will be available for Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears in Week 3. Barkley was a limited participant in practice on Thursday before upgrading to full practice participation on Friday. According to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer, Barkley said on Thursday that he had an MRI that "went well." On Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reported that Barkley said he was "feeling good" this week and that he will wear a cowboy collar to help protect his neck. Barkley got hurt in the first quarter of the game against the Titans and eventually returned, but played just 12 snaps in Week 2. He totaled four carries for just nine yards, while adding one reception (on two targets) for 11 yards against Tennessee. Barkley played 39 snaps in a 24-22 Week 1 victory over the Washington Commanders. Barkley will face a Chicago defense that is giving up 122 rushing yards per game (22nd in the NFL) through two weeks. Through two games in 2026, Barkley has tallied 19 carries for 92 yards (4.8 yards per attempt) and two catches for eight yards. He is yet to find the end zone. Barkley is averaging 3.5 yards after contact per rush. If fully healthy, expect Barkley to get a full workload. He ranks as RotoBaller's No. 9 running back for Week 3, has a strong matchup rating of 115.7 and is projected to score 14.4 fantasy points. Fantasy managers can safely place Barkley in their lineups for Week 3.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Set to Face Bears on Monday
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) will play Monday night against Chicago, according to Andrew DiCecco. Barkley was limited Thursday before practicing in full Friday, and he said that he expected to be ready. The stinger knocked him out early against Tennessee, but he returned in the third quarter and finished with four carries for nine yards plus one catch for 11 yards. Philadelphia leaned on Tank Bigsby while Barkley was out, but that shouldn't be necessary this week. Barkley is set to be back in his usual lead role Monday night.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Full practice Friday
metadata.description: Barkley (stinger) was a full practice participant Friday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley's status for Week 3 was chief among the health concerns coming out of a Week 2 win at Tennessee in which he suffered a stinger and missed most of the first half. After kicking off this week with a limited practice Thursday, he handled every practice rep one day later, indicating he's good to go for Monday's contest in Chicago. Having said that, Barkley told Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia on Friday that he'll wear protective gear around his neck and shoulders this week and perhaps as long as symptoms of the stinger are impacting him.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Will wear protective gear Monday
metadata.description: Barkley (stinger) said Friday that he's "feeling good" this week and will wear protective gear around his neck during Monday's contest at Chicago, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley also relayed that he underwent an MRI earlier this week on his left shoulder to ensure there wasn't additional damage after he sustained a stinger in this past Sunday's win in Tennessee. He officially was a limited participant Thursday and took part in Friday's session, but unless he logs a full practice either Friday or Saturday, he seems destined to be tagged with a designation ahead of Week 3 action.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley to Wear Neck Collar on Monday Night
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (neck) said he is feeling good this week and will be wearing a neck cowboy collar on Monday night in the Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears, according to Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports. Barkley underwent an MRI exam early this week to make sure there was no additional damage in his neck/shoulder after he suffered a stinger in the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. The Eagles listed Barkley as limited in practice on Thursday, but he was able to upgrade to full on Friday, suggesting he could be cleared from the final Week 3 injury report on Saturday. Backup Tank Bigsby (abdomen) came out of Sunday's game with an abdomen issue, but he was able to return to a limited practice on Friday after being held out on Thursday. Barkley gave his fantasy managers a dud in Week 2 with only four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards, but he will be back in must-start territory against the Bears on Monday night now that he has recovered from the stinger he suffered on Sunday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Practicing again Friday
metadata.description: Barkley (stinger) is taking part in the open portion of Friday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley is stacking practices in the wake of the stinger that he sustained during a Week 2 win at Tennessee, going down as a limited participant to begin Week 3 prep and likely to be listed as at least that Friday. He told Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer on Thursday that an MRI on his left shoulder "went well," and the running back also was seen wearing a protective device on his shoulder and neck area at the ensuing session. With Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) also on the injury report this week, the situation in the Eagles backfield will be monitored to get a sense of who may be able to play Monday in Chicago.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) practices Friday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley practiced again on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley remains on track to be good to go for Monday's game against the Bears.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Officially limited Thursday
metadata.description: Barkley (stinger) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Barkley missed most of the first half of the Eagles' Week 2 win at Tennessee due to a stinger, but he returned in the second half and ended the contest with five touches for 20 yards from scrimmage. He told Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer on Thursday that an MRI on his left shoulder "went well," and during the corresponding session he was spotted wearing a protective device on his shoulder and neck area, per Zach Berman of The Athletic. Barkley is actually the healthiest of the running backs on Philadelphia's active roster, as both Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and Will Shipley (foot) were held out of drills entirely to begin Week 3 prep. The overall situation bears monitoring in the coming days to see who among the trio will be available Monday in Chicago.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) expects to play Monday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley (stinger) told reporters that his MRI went well and he expects to play on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: Barkley underwent an MRI after suffering a stinger in last week's win over the Titans, but the results were apparently good and he reportedly expects to play on Monday night against the Bears. Fantasy managers should still keep close tabs on his status throughout the rest of the week to ensure that will be the case.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Recent MRI 'went well'
metadata.description: Barkley (shoulder) said Thursday that his MRI "went well" when asked about his chances of playing in Monday's game at Chicago, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley departed after the Eagles' first offensive snap this past Sunday at Tennessee and was diagnosed with a stinger, but he returned after halftime and finished Week 2 with four carries for nine yards and one catch (on two targets) for 11 yards. Because the Eagles play the Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 3, Philadelphia didn't hold practice until Thursday this week, and Barkley was seen wearing a protective device on his shoulder and neck area during the open portion of that session, per Zach Berman of The Athletic. Barkley's activity level will become known once the team posts its first injury report of the week.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Taking part in practice
metadata.description: Barkley (shoulder) is taking part in practice Thursday while sporting a protective device on his shoulder and neck area, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley is wearing a "cowboy collar," which is a molded foam protection device that prevents the head from jerking backward. He missed a chunk of this past Sunday's win over the Titans due to a stinger in his shoulder and neck area, so it's encouraging that Barkley is participating in practice Thursday, though it remains to be seen if he'll be listed as a full or limited participant. The Eagles play on Monday Night Football in Week 3 against the Bears, who face an uncertain quarterback situation.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Says his "MRI Went Well"
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (neck, shoulder), who was seen practicing on Thursday, said that his "MRI went well" when asked about his prospects for playing on Monday night in Week 3 against the Chicago Bears, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. McLane was also told that Barkley expects to play against the Bears. He will most likely go down as a limited participant in the team's first official practice of the week after suffering a stinger and missing plenty of game time before eventually returning in the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans. The 29-year-old three-time Pro Bowler only had four carries for nine yards and caught one of his two targets for 11 yards in the passing game, with backup Tank Bigsby outproducing him on the day. All signs point to Barkley being ready for this Sunday's game against the Bears on Monday night, but fantasy managers will want to keep an eye on his status over the next couple of days. If active against Chicago, Barkley will be a must-start in all fantasy lineups. UPDATE: Barkley was officially limited in practice on Thursday.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) without update per HC Nick Sirianni
metadata.description: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not have an update on the status of Saquon Barkley on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The Eagles injury report will be released later in the afternoon. Tank Bigsby is worth stashing for now for fantasy managers just in case with Barkley.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Status still muddled for Week 3
metadata.description: Head coach Nick Sirianni said Thursday that he had no update on the status of Barkley (shoulder) heading into the Eagles' first practice of the week, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Sirianni noted that the Eagles will release their initial Week 3 injury report following Thursday's practice, when it will be known whether Barkley is operating with any restrictions after he dealt with a stinger during this past Sunday's win over the Titans. The stinger kept him out for most of the first half, but he returned to the field for the start of the third quarter. However, Barkley didn't operate as a three-down player for the rest of that contest, finishing with four carries for nine yards to go with an 11-yard reception on two targets over just 12 total snaps.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Expects to Play Monday
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) was suited up and on the practice field Thursday, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. McLane added that Barkley expects to play Monday night against Chicago, though the Eagles had not yet released his official participation level. Barkley suffered the stinger on Philadelphia's first offensive play against Tennessee and missed most of the first half before returning in the third quarter. He finished with four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards. Barkley has 19 carries for 92 yards through two games. Getting back on the field Thursday is an encouraging sign, but his practice designation and how he responds over the next few days will matter before his Week 3 status is settled.

metadata.title: No Update on Saquon Barkley With Week 3 Looming
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said on Thursday that he did not have an update on running back Saquon Barkley (neck, shoulder), who missed some game time in the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday after suffering a stinger, according to Zach Berman of The Athletic. The Eagles have a practice on Thursday, so we will know shortly whether or not he was on the field. Although Barkley eventually returned to the game on Sunday, he finished with only four carries for nine yards and had one catch for an 11-yard gain. Meanwhile, backup Tank Bigsby had 13 carries for 33 yards and a touchdown while adding two receptions for five yards. The 29-year-old Barkley has a lengthy injury history, so the Eagles could mix in more of Bigsby to take some of the load off if Barkley is active this weekend for a matchup on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears on the road. Bigsby should have been one of the more popular waiver-wire pickups after Week 2, but he is still only rostered in 39% of Yahoo leagues. He would have major fantasy upside if Barkley does miss any time in 2026, making him a valuable bench stash right now.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley Likely Avoided a Serious Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) missed a portion of Sunday's Week 2 contest against the Tennessee Titans. According to Ian Rapoport, the injury is not believed to be serious, but he will still undergo an MRI on Monday as a precaution. Barkley exited during the first half of the victory, and while he did return later on, the team limited his workload. He finished Week 2 with just 20 scrimmage yards on five total touches, ceding work to Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley. So far, it seems like Barkley merely suffered a stinger, which is an uncomfortable but non-serious injury that occurs when a player pinches a nerve. Stingers rarely require players to miss extended time, so if the MRI rules out any structural damage, we'd expect to see Barkley back in his every-down role next week against the Chicago Bears.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Slated for MRI on shoulder stinger
metadata.description: Barkley said after Sunday's 24-20 win at Tennessee that he feels "alright," but he'll undergo an MRI after missing a portion of the game due to a stinger, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley was diagnosed with a stinger after the Eagles' first offensive play of the game and missed the rest of the first half, but he was able to return after halftime, finishing with four carries for nine yards and one catch (on two targets) for 11 yards. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby paced the backfield with 15 touches for 38 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD, and fellow RB Will Shipley turned nine touches into 29 total yards. If Barkley ends up missing any time, Bigsby likely would be the primary beneficiary, but Shipley also figures to have a role in Philadelphia's offense.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley held to nine yards while surviving injury scare
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley carried the ball four times for nine yards while catching one of his two targets for 11 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Barkley missed some time with a shoulder stinger but ultimately was able to return to the game, which explains his quiet afternoon at the office. The veteran running back has now run for 92 scoreless yards on the season as he looks to bounce back ahead of a Week 3 road matchup against the Bears. Assuming his shoulder is okay, Barkley will check in as a low-end RB1 in fantasy for that matchup.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) returns to the game
metadata.description: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) has returned to the game in the second half against the Titans.
metadata.analysis: Barkley was seen on the sidelines holding his helmet after his first half injury and he did not return prior to halftime. Barkley took a carry in the third quarter and appears poised to return as the primary running back for the remainder of the game.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Checks back into Sunday's game
metadata.description: Barkley (shoulder) returned to Sunday's game against the Titans for the start of the third quarter, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: After suffering a stinger on a carry for no gain on the Eagles' first offensive snap, Barkley sat out the rest of the first half while making trips to the medical tent on the sideline as well as the locker room. The Eagles had listed Barkley as questionable to return, and the running back apparently responded well enough to treatment for the team to send him back on the field to begin the second half.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley (stinger) questionable to return Sunday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley (stinger) is questionable to return for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Tennessee Titans Sunday according to Mike Garafolo.
metadata.analysis: Barkley suffered the injury early in the first quarter for the Eagles, with Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley taking over the backfield for head coach Nick Sirianni against the Titans.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Questionable to return to Week 2
metadata.description: The Eagles announced that Barkley (neck/shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans due to a stinger.
metadata.analysis: Barkley appeared to be favoring his neck and left shoulder after he was tackled to the ground on a carry during the Eagles' first offensive play of the game. The running back headed to the locker room shortly after the play in question and is receiving further treatment for the injury while the Eagles determine whether or not he's able to return. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley will likely share work out of the backfield if Barkley ends up being shut down for the rest of the contest.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley - Tending to left arm injury
metadata.description: Barkley headed to the locker room during the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Titans to be evaluated for an apparent left arm injury, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Barkley sustained the injury on a zero-yard carry on the Eagles' first offensive play of the game. After a brief trip to the medical tent on the sideline, Barkley jogged back to the locker room to be checked out further. The Eagles should have an update on the star running back's status shortly.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley heads to locker room Sunday
metadata.description: Saquon Barkley exited Sunday's contest for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Tennessee Titans with an apparent arm injury according to Ari Meirov.

metadata.title: Saquon Barkley to Get MRI After Stinger in Week 2
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) said he will get an MRI and "know more in the future" after being injured on Sunday in a 24-20 win against the Tennessee Titans, ESPN's Tim McManus reported via the X platform. Barkley left after his first carry of the game and was questionable to return, although he took to the field for the Eagles' first drive of the second half. He ended the day with just four carries for nine yards. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley led the backfield in Sunday's road tilt in Barkley's absence, with Bigsby recording 13 carries for 33 yards and a touchdown.
